2608.24545.title: Discovering Adaptive Transmission Programs for Collective Innovation
2608.24545.paper_summary: Human collective intelligence depends on transmission processes: who shares what with whom, how, and when. While these processes emerge from individual cognition, they can also be directed by deliberate top-down protocols. Prior work has studied how transmission shapes collective outcomes primarily through the lens of network structure, varying who shares with whom and when. But networks are state-agnostic: they cannot condition transmission on what agents know or on the state of the collective. Here, we formalize transmission protocols as state-aware programs that route information and resources based on agent and collective states, and we use LLM-guided evolutionary search to design effective protocols in a collective discovery task. Evolved protocols increase collective performance over standard baselines from the literature by up to 37%. Ablations confirm that state-awareness drives this advantage: removing content-dependence while preserving network topology and timing eliminates performance gains. We find that evolved protocols also transfer across domain variations and agent populations. These results demonstrate that effective and generalizable transmission protocols can be discovered in silico, suggesting a path toward AI-assisted design of coordination infrastructure that enhances human collective intelligence.
2608.24545.paper_summary_zh: 人類的集體智慧依賴於傳輸過程：誰與誰分享什麼，如何分享，以及何時分享。雖然這些過程源於個體的認知，但也可以通過有意的自上而下的協議來指導。先前的研究主要通過網絡結構的視角研究了傳輸如何塑造集體結果，變化的是誰與誰分享以及何時分享。但網絡是無狀態的：它們無法根據代理的知識或集體的狀態來調節傳輸。在這裡，我們將傳輸協議形式化為狀態感知的程序，根據代理和集體狀態路由信息和資源，並使用LLM引導的進化搜索來設計集體發現任務中的有效協議。進化的協議在文獻中的標準基準上提高了集體表現，最高可達37%。消融實驗確認了狀態感知驅動了這一優勢：在保持網絡拓撲和時序的情況下去除內容依賴性會消除性能增益。我們發現進化的協議也能跨域變化和代理人群體轉移。這些結果表明，可以在計算機中發現有效且可通用的傳輸協議，為增強人類集體智慧的協調基礎設施的AI輔助設計提供了一條途徑。
